questions.question: Pandit Chhannulal Mishra, who passed away at the age of 89, was associated with which of the following Hindustani classical music gharanas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banaras Gharana**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Pandit Chhannulal Mishra** is a preeminent exponent of the **Banaras Gharana** of **Hindustani classical music**, globally recognized for his mastery over the **Purab Ang Gayaki**.

• Born in **1936** in the **Azamgarh** district of **Uttar Pradesh**, he later moved to **Varanasi** (Banaras), which became the spiritual and musical foundation of his career.

• His musical lineage is unique as he initially received training in the **Kirana Gharana** style under **Ustad Abdul Ghani Khan**, but he later specialized in the **Banaras** style under the guidance of **Thakur Jaidev Singh**.

• He is exceptionally versatile, performing a wide array of genres including **Khayal**, **Thumri**, **Dadra**, **Kajri**, **Hori**, **Chaiti**, and **Bhajans**, often blending classical rigor with folk traditions.

• In recognition of his immense contribution to Indian classical music, he was conferred with the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2020**, the **Padma Bhushan** in **2010**, and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Agra Gharana**

• Founded by **Haji Sujan Khan** and later revitalized by **Ustad Faiyaz Khan** (also known as **Prempiya**).

• Characterized by a deep emphasis on **Layakari** (rhythmic play) and the **Nom-Tom Alap**, often showing a strong influence of **Dhrupad-Dhamar**.

• **Gwalior Gharana**

• Considered the **oldest** khayal-based gharana, established under the patronage of the **Maratha kings**.

• Founded by legends like **Nathan Khan** and **Peer Baksh**, it focuses on **lucidity**, **straight-line (Sapat) Taans**, and **Behlawa**.

• **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana**

• Established by **Ustad Alladiya Khan**, this style is famous for its complexity and the use of **Aprachalit** (rare) and **Jod** (compound) ragas.

• It maintains a steady **medium-tempo (Madhyalaya)** and features intricate, spiral-like **Taan** patterns.

</ul

questions.question: The Kol Uprising, which resisted British law and order intervention, took place in which region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chotanagpur**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Kol Uprising** was a significant tribal revolt that took place between **1831** and **1832** in the **Chotanagpur** plateau, which spans modern-day **Jharkhand** and parts of **Odisha** and **West Bengal**.

• The rebellion was primarily triggered by the **British East India Company** policy of transferring traditional tribal lands to non-tribal outsiders, including **Sikh** and **Muslim** farmers, and the introduction of oppressive land revenue systems.

• The uprising involved several tribal communities, notably the **Mundas**, **Oraons**, **Hos**, and **Bhumi**, who collectively resisted the exploitation by money-lenders (**Mahajans**) and local British officials.

• Prominent leaders of the movement included **Buddhu Bhagat**, **Joa Bhagat**, and **Madara Mahato**, who organized armed resistance against British military intervention and law enforcement.

• The revolt was characterized by the targeting of colonial infrastructure and outsiders (referred to as **Dikus**), but it was eventually suppressed by superior British military forces after significant loss of life.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Mysore**:

• Primarily known for the **Anglo-Mysore Wars** (1767−1799) involving **Haidar Ali** and **Tipu Sultan**, and the peasant-led **Nagar Rebellion** of **1830**.

• **Awadh**:

• A major center of the **Indian Rebellion of 1857** following its **1856 annexation** by **Lord Dalhousie** under the pretext of misgovernance.

• **Bengal**:

• Witnessed various early anti-British movements such as the **Sanyasi Rebellion** (1763−1800), the **Indigo Revolt** (1859), and the **Santal Rebellion** (1855−1856).

</ul

questions.question: Which folk music tradition from West Bengal, associated with spiritual themes, is performed by wandering minstrels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baul**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Baul** music is a distinct folk tradition originating from **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**, representing a unique spiritual synthesis of **Vaishnavism**, **Sahajayana Buddhism**, and **Sufi** mysticism.

• The term is derived from the **Sanskrit** word **Vatula**, meaning 'divinely mad' or 'inspired', referring to the wandering minstrels who renounce social norms to seek the 'Maner Manush' (the Man of the Heart) within.

• In **2005**, the **Baul tradition** was officially recognized by **UNESCO** and included in the list of **Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity**.

• The performances are characterized by simple yet profound lyrics, often accompanied by traditional instruments like the **Ektara** (one-stringed lute), **Khomok**, **Duggi**, and **Ghungur**.

• Historically, **Lalon Shah** (Lalon Fakir) is considered the most influential saint-composer of this tradition, having composed thousands of songs that preach religious harmony and humanity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Pandavani**:

• This is a narrative folk ballad form from **Chhattisgarh** that depicts the lives of the **Pandavas** from the **Mahabharata**.

• It is performed in two styles: **Vedamati** and **Kapalik**, with **Teejan Bai** being its most world-renowned exponent.

• **Alha**:

• This is a heroic poetic tradition popular in the **Bundelkhand** region of **Uttar Pradesh** and **Madhya Pradesh**.

• The songs narrate the **52 battles** fought by the legendary warrior brothers **Alha** and **Udal** during the **12th century**.

• **Bhavai**:

• A popular folk theatre form of **Gujarat** and **Rajasthan**, traditionally performed by the **Targala** community.

• It combines music, dance, and satirical dialogue to address social issues, often involving performers balancing multiple **earthen pots** on their heads.

</ul

questions.question: The Constitution of India prohibits which of the following types of citizenship?

options.text: Citizenship by registration under statutory provisions
Dual citizenship of another country along with Indian citizenship
Citizenship by birth within the territory of India
Citizenship by naturalisation after fulfilling prescribed conditions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dual citizenship of another country along with Indian citizenship**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Article 9** of the **Constitution of India** explicitly states that any person who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a **foreign State** shall cease to be a citizen of India. This fundamental provision prohibits the concept of **dual citizenship**.

• India adopts a **Single Citizenship** policy, which is a feature borrowed from the **British Constitution**, ensuring that citizens owe their full allegiance only to the **Indian Union** regardless of their state of residence.

• The **Citizenship Act, 1955**, provides for the termination of citizenship under **Section 9** if an individual acquires the nationality of another country, reinforcing the constitutional prohibition.

• Unlike federal structures like the **United States** where citizens may hold both state and national citizenship, the **Indian Constitution** does not recognize separate state citizenship, maintaining national unity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **Citizenship Act of 1955** prescribes five ways to acquire Indian citizenship:

• **Birth**: Acquisition based on being born within the **territory of India** (Section 3).

• **Descent**: Acquisition based on Indian parentage for those born outside India (Section 4).

• **Registration**: A process for **Persons of Indian Origin (PIO)** or spouses of Indian citizens who have resided in India for a specified period (Section 5).

• **Naturalisation**: A process for foreigners who have resided in India for **12 years** and fulfill criteria in the **Third Schedule** (Section 6).

• **Incorporation of Territory**: If a new territory becomes part of India, the **Government of India** specifies the persons who shall be citizens (Section 7).

• The **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI)** scheme, introduced via the **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2005**, provides certain residency and travel benefits to the diaspora but does not grant **voting rights**, political office, or true **dual nationality**.
</ul

questions.question: When and where did the first session of the Indian National Congress take place?

questions.question: As per Article 280(1) of the Constitution, the Finance Commission is to be constituted:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Every five years or earlier**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Article 280(1)** of the **Constitution of India** mandates the establishment of a **Finance Commission** as a **quasi-judicial body**.

• The provision specifies that the **President of India** shall constitute the commission within **two years** from the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of **every fifth year** or at such **earlier time** as the President considers necessary.

• The primary mandate of the commission is to address the **vertical** and **horizontal imbalances** in the distribution of financial resources between the **Union** and the **States**.

• The **Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951**, further outlines the qualifications, appointment, and powers of the commission members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Composition of the Commission**:

• It consists of a **Chairman** and **four other members** appointed by the **President of India**.

• The **Chairman** should be a person having experience in **public affairs**.

• The **Parliament** determines the qualifications of the members, which typically include expertise in **finance**, **economics**, or **judicial matters** (specifically a **High Court Judge** or someone qualified for such an appointment).

• **Major Functions**:

• Recommending the distribution of **net proceeds of taxes** between the Center and the States.

• Determining the principles governing **Grants-in-aid** to the States from the **Consolidated Fund of India** under **Article 275**.

• Suggesting measures to augment the **Consolidated Fund of a State** to support **Panchayats** and **Municipalities** based on the recommendations of the **State Finance Commission**.

• **Current Status**:

• The **16th Finance Commission** has been constituted under the chairmanship of **Arvind Panagariya**, with its recommendations expected to cover the five-year period starting **April 1, 2026**.

</ul

questions.question: Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan was sworn in as _____ Vice President of India.

 **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a key component of the 1991 industrial reforms in India?

options.text: Expansion of the public sector in key industries
Abolition of the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Expansion of the public sector in key industries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **New Industrial Policy (NIP)** was announced on **July 24, 1991**, under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh** to pull the Indian economy out of a severe **balance of payments crisis**.

• A primary objective of the **1991 reforms** was the **contraction**, not the expansion, of the public sector; the number of industries reserved exclusively for the **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** was drastically reduced from **17** to **8**.

• The policy shifted focus towards **Privatization** and **Disinvestment**, where the government began selling its equity in public enterprises to private investors and the general public to improve efficiency and accountability.

• **Industrial Delicensing** was a cornerstone of the reforms, where the requirement for obtaining government licenses was abolished for all but **18 industries** related to security, strategic concerns, and social reasons.

• The **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act** was significantly modified to remove the **asset threshold limit**, which previously required large industrial houses to seek government permission for any expansion or diversification.

• The reforms introduced **Globalization** by facilitating **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, allowing automatic approval for up to **51%** foreign equity in high-priority industries to attract foreign capital and advanced technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**

• Goal: To increase **international competitiveness** and technology transfer.

• Evolution: Over time, the limit has been increased to **100%** in several sectors like **telecom** and **civil aviation**.

• **MRTP Act and Competition Act**

• Historical Context: Enacted in **1969** to prevent the concentration of economic power.

• Reform: The **MRTP Commission** shifted its focus from controlling size to controlling **unfair trade practices**, eventually leading to the **Competition Act, 2002**.

• **Industrial Licensing**

• Current Status: Currently, licensing is mandatory for only a handful of sectors, including **electronic aerospace**, **defense equipment**, **hazardous chemicals**, and **industrial explosives**.

• **Public Sector Reservation**

• Current Status: Only **Atomic Energy** and **Railway Operations** (excluding certain infrastructure components) remain exclusively under the central government's control today.

</ul

242 = ?

The final value of the equation is **242**.

The correct answer is **option 1**

• **Left turn and 12 km:** Turning **left** from **West** means he is now traveling **South**. He drives 12 km.

• **Left turn and 9 km:** Turning **left** from **South** means he is now traveling **East**. He drives 9 km.

• **Final left turn and 2 km:** Turning **left** from **East** means he is now traveling **North**. He drives 2 km and stops at **Point P**.

 **Calculation**

**Step 2:** Place **O** and **R**.

**O** plays immediately before **R**. Possible consecutive slots remaining are (**Monday, Tuesday**) or (**Thursday, Friday**). However, it is given that **O** cannot play on **Thursday**. Therefore, **O** must play on **Monday** and **R** must play on **Tuesday**.

**Step 3:** Place **N, S,** and **P**.

The remaining days are **Thursday, Friday,** and **Sunday**. There must be two persons between **N** and **S**. The only way to have two persons between two days from the remaining set (**Thursday, Friday, Sunday**) and the already filled **Saturday** is to place **N** and **S** on **Thursday** and **Sunday**. Between **Thursday** and **Sunday** are **Friday** and **Saturday** (two people).

Since **N** does not play on **Sunday**, **N** must play on **Thursday** and **S** plays on **Sunday**. This leaves **Friday** for **P**.

questions.question: What is the difference between Reply and Forward in email?

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

 __
 
• The **Reply__** function is used to send a response back to the **__original sender__** of the email.

 __
 
• The **Forward__** function allows a user to send the content of an existing email to a **__new recipient__** who was not part of the original thread.
 
• Unlike Reply, the **__recipient field__** is left blank, and the user must manually enter the email address of the person they wish to share the information with.
 
• It is commonly used to pass on **__attachments__** or information to a third party.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

 __
 
• This option sends a response to the **original sender__** and every other person included in the **__"To"__** and **__"Cc"__** fields of the original email.
 
• It is used to keep all stakeholders involved in a **__group discussion__** updated simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **__Cc (Carbon Copy)__**
 __
 
• Used to send a copy of the email to people who need to stay **informed__** but are not the primary recipients.
 
• All recipients can **__see__** the email addresses listed in the Cc field.

 __
 
• Allows a user to send a copy of the email to recipients without their addresses being **visible__** to others.
 
• This is often used for **__privacy__** or when sending an email to a large distribution list.

questions.question: In a switched Ethernet LAN, which switching method begins forwarding a frame as soon as the destination MAC address is read, resulting in the lowest latency but higher risk of forwarding corrupted frames?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __Cut-Through Switching__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Cut-Through Switching__**

 __
 
• Starts the forwarding process immediately after the **destination MAC address__** (the first 6 bytes of the frame) is identified.
 
• It offers the **__lowest latency__** because the switch does not wait for the entire frame to arrive before transmitting it to the destination port.
 
• A major disadvantage is that it does not perform a **__Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC)__**, lead
 
• 41
 
• ing to a higher risk of forwarding **__corrupted frames__** or **__runts__**.
 
• It is primarily used in high-performance environments where speed is prioritized over error-free transmission at the switch level.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Store-and-Forward Switching__**

 __
 
• The switch receives and stores the **entire frame__** in a buffer before forwarding.
 
• It performs a **__CRC check__** to ensure the frame is not corrupted; if an error is detected, the frame is discarded.
 
• This method ensures high reliability but results in **__higher latency__** proportional to the frame size.
 
 
 
• **__Fragment-Free Switching__**
 __
 
• This is a modified version of cut-through switching that waits to receive the first **64 bytes__** of a frame before forwarding.
 
• It filters out **__collision fragments__** (which are usually less than 64 bytes) while still maintaining lower latency than store-and-forward.
 
• It provides a balance between **__error checking__** and speed.
 
 
 
• **__Token Passing__**
 __
 
• This is a **channel access method__** used in architectures like **__Token Ring__** and FDDI, rather than a method of frame switching in modern Ethernet.
 
• It involves a special frame called a **__token__** that is passed between nodes to grant permission to transmit data.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of PCB in a computer system?

options.text: An input device for transferring data
A physical board connecting electronic components
A protocol used in wireless networks
A software tool for virus removal

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __A physical board connecting electronic components__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Printed Circuit Board (PCB)__**

 __
 
• A PCB is a physical structure that **mechanically supports__** and **__electrically connects__** electronic components.
 
• It uses **__conductive pathways__**, tracks, or signal traces etched from copper sheets laminated onto a non-conductive substrate.
 
• In a computer system, the **__motherboard__** is the most significant PCB, acting as the main hub for communication between components.
 
• Components like **__resistors__**, **__capacitors__**, and **__integrated circuits__** are typically **__soldered__** onto the PCB to secure them and create circuits.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Composition and Layers__**

 __
 
• Common substrate materials include **FR-4__** (a fiberglass-reinforced epoxy laminate), which provides insulation.
 
• PCBs can be **__single-sided__**, **__double-sided__**, or **__multi-layered__** to accommodate complex high-speed computer circuitry.
 
 
 
• **__Manufacturing Technologies__**
 __
 
• **Surface Mount Technology (SMT)__**: A method where components are placed directly onto the surface of the board, allowing for smaller computer parts.
 
• **__Through-Hole Technology__**: An older method where component leads are inserted into holes drilled in the **__PCB__**.
 
 
 
• **__Role in Computers__**
 __
 
• Beyond the motherboard, PCBs are found in **Graphics Cards (GPUs)__**, **__Network Interface Cards (NICs)__**, and **__RAM modules__**.
 
• They ensure stable **__power distribution__** and high-speed **__data signal__** integrity across the system.

 __

• Users can choose the **__Create from file__** option to browse and select existing documents or spreadsheets.

 __
 
• **Linking__**: The object in PowerPoint updates automatically whenever the **__source file__** in Word or Excel is modified.

⇒ P(E ∪ F) = 1/6 + 1/2 = 4/6 = 2/3.

The probability of **not E and not F** is the complement of the union: 1 − P(E ∪ F).

⇒ 1 − 2/3 = 1/3.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Probability of event E, P(E) = 1/6

Probability of event F, P(F) = 1/2

Events E and F are **mutually exclusive**.

**Formula Used:**

1. Addition Theorem: P(E ∪ F) = P(E) + P(F) − P(E ∩ F)

2. De Morgan's Law: P(E' ∩ F') = P((E ∪ F)') = 1 − P(E ∪ F)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98d36e291e9ece0854c8f24a105b20ba3ccdd1ec9528a543ad17f2dc0948c9ae.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since E and F are **mutually exclusive**, P(E ∩ F) = 0.

⇒ P(E ∪ F) = P(E) + P(F) = 1/6 + 1/2

⇒ P(E ∪ F) = 1/6 + 3/6 = 4/6 = 2/3.

⇒ P(not E and not F) = P(E' ∩ F')

⇒ P(E' ∩ F') = 1 − P(E ∪ F)

⇒ P(E' ∩ F') = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mutually Exclusive Events

Events that cannot occur at the same time are called **mutually exclusive**. For such events, the intersection P(A ∩ B) = 0.

De Morgan's Laws in Probability

P(A' ∩ B') = P((A ∪ B)') = 1 − P(A ∪ B) and P(A' ∪ B') = P((A ∩ B)') = 1 − P(A ∩ B).

Independent Events

Two events are **independent** if the occurrence of one does not affect the other, defined by P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).

Complementary Events

The **complement** of an event E, denoted as E' or Ec, contains all outcomes in the sample space that are not in E, such that P(E) + P(E') = 1.</p

questions.question: The coordinates of the centroid of the triangle ABC whose vertices are A(-16, 13), B(-2, -9) and C(2, 13), is

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **centroid** G(x, y) of a **triangle** is the average of its vertices coordinates: ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3).

x-coordinate = (−16 − 2 + 2) ÷ 3 = −16/3

y-coordinate = (13 − 9 + 13) ÷ 3 = 17/3

**∴ The correct answer is (-(16)/(3), (17)/(3)).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Vertices of **triangle ABC** are **A(−16, 13)**, **B(−2, −9)**, and **C(2, 13)**.

**Formula Used:** Centroid (G) = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/15a7ff20c8dcb3690524da44c0ff514ebf623a0e01a7abe1aabb15afb9547245.png] 

Let the coordinates of the **centroid** be (x, y).

⇒ x = (x₁ + x₂ + x₃) ÷ 3

⇒ x = (−16 + (−2) + 2) ÷ 3

⇒ x = −16 ÷ 3

⇒ y = (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) ÷ 3

⇒ y = (13 + (−9) + 13) ÷ 3

⇒ y = 17 ÷ 3

∴ Coordinates of **centroid** = (−16/3, 17/3)

**∴ The correct answer is (-(16)/(3), (17)/(3)).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Centroid

The **centroid** of a triangle is the point of concurrency of its **medians** and always lies inside the triangle.

Section Ratio

The **centroid** divides each **median** in the ratio **2 : 1** from the vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

Area of Triangle

The area of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), and (x₃, y₃) is 1/2 |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|.

questions.question: Simplify (2.5 times 0.48 div 0.6) + (3.5 + 1.6 div 0.8) - (4.8 times 0.25 div 0.8) .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the expression by breaking it into three independent terms separated by **addition** and **subtraction** signs.

First term: (2.5 × 0.48 ÷ 0.6) = (1.2 ÷ 0.6) = 2

Second term: (3.5 + 1.6 ÷ 0.8) = (3.5 + 2) = 5.5

Third term: (4.8 × 0.25 ÷ 0.8) = (1.2 ÷ 0.8) = 1.5

Combined result: 2 + 5.5 − 1.5 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (2.5 × 0.48 ÷ 0.6) + (3.5 + 1.6 ÷ 0.8) − (4.8 × 0.25 ÷ 0.8)

**Formula Used:**

Apply the **VBODMAS** rule: **V**inculum, **B**rackets, **O**f, **D**ivision, **M**ultiplication, **A**ddition, and **S**ubtraction.

**Calculation:**

⇒ (2.5 × 0.48 ÷ 0.6) + (3.5 + 1.6 ÷ 0.8) − (4.8 × 0.25 ÷ 0.8)

Solving the first bracket:

⇒ (1.2 ÷ 0.6) = 2

Solving the second bracket (priority to **division**):

⇒ (3.5 + 2) = 5.5

Solving the third bracket:

⇒ (1.2 ÷ 0.8) = 1.5

Now, combining all the results:

⇒ 2 + 5.5 − 1.5 ⇒ 7.5 − 1.5 ⇒ 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Principle

The rule defines the correct order of operations as **Brackets** (), **Orders** (roots/exponents), **Division** and **Multiplication** (left to right), and finally **Addition** and **Subtraction**.

Decimal Division Shortcut

When dividing decimals like 1.6 ÷ 0.8, you can remove the decimal by multiplying both numbers by 10, converting it to a simpler integer division: 16 ÷ 8 = 2.

Multiplication by 0.25

Multiplying a number by **0.25** is equivalent to dividing the number by 4. For example, 4.8 × 0.25 = 4.8 ÷ 4 = 1.2.

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers, each having three digits, is 19 and their LCM is 760. The number of such pairs is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**HCF** = 19 and **LCM** = 760.

Product of co-prime factors (a × b) = LCM ÷ HCF = 760 ÷ 19 = 40.

Possible **co-prime pairs** (a, b) such that a × b = 40 are (1, 40) and (5, 8).

For (1, 40), numbers are 19 × 1 = 19 and 19 × 40 = 760. (19 is a **2-digit number**).

For (5, 8), numbers are 19 × 5 = 95 and 19 × 8 = 152. (95 is a **2-digit number**).

No pair satisfies the **three-digit number** constraint for both numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF of two numbers = 19

LCM of two numbers = 760

Constraint: Both numbers must have **three digits** (100 to 999).

**Formula used:**

LCM = HCF × a × b (where a and b are co-prime integers)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6801aed1cf1910a2a8f03cc878b5a8f9044d35960360395e342ed9d88a712fc.png] 

⇒ Let the numbers be 19a and 19b.

⇒ 19 × a × b = 760

⇒ a × b = 760 ÷ 19 = 40

⇒ Co-prime pairs (a, b) that multiply to 40 are:

⇒ Case 1: a = 1, b = 40

⇒ Numbers: 19 × 1 = 19 and 19 × 40 = 760. (19 is not a 3-digit number).

⇒ Case 2: a = 5, b = 8

⇒ Numbers: 19 × 5 = 95 and 19 × 8 = 152. (95 is not a 3-digit number).

⇒ In both cases, at least one number is a **two-digit number**.

⇒ Thus, the number of such **three-digit pairs** is 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental HCF-LCM Relation

For any two numbers x and y, x × y = HCF(x, y) × LCM(x, y).

Co-prime Factors

If HCF is h, the numbers can be written as ha and hb, where HCF(a, b) = 1. The LCM is then h × a × b.

HCF Divisibility Rule

The HCF of a set of numbers must always be a factor of their LCM. If LCM ÷ HCF is not an integer, no such numbers can exist.

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl has (992 pi)/(3) { cm}³ of water in it. If a ball of radius 2 cm is dropped into the bowl, the water level is raised up to the height of the bowl without any extra spillage of water out of the bowl. What is the radius of the bowl?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **total volume** of the bowl is the sum of the **initial water volume** and the **volume of the ball**.

Combined Volume = 992π/3 + (4/3)π × (2)³ = 992π/3 + 32π/3 = 1024π/3 cm³.

Since the bowl is a hemisphere: (2/3)πR³ = 1024π/3.

⇒ 2R³ = 1024 ⇒ R³ = 512 ⇒ R = 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **volume of water** in the bowl = 992π/3 cm³

**Radius of the ball** (r) = 2 cm

**Formula Used:**

1. **Volume of a sphere** = (4/3)πr³

2. **Volume of a hemisphere** = (2/3)πR³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61e68071c99fa94d6be7484c376798137f9c0a90d1a9acc3d77b0ab97868c0b1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of the ball dropped = (4/3) × π × (2)³

⇒ Volume of the ball = (4/3) × π × 8 = 32π/3 cm³

⇒ Since the water level rises to the brim, Total Volume of Bowl = Volume of Water + Volume of Ball

⇒ Total Volume of Bowl = 992π/3 + 32π/3 = 1024π/3 cm³

⇒ (2/3)πR³ = 1024π/3

⇒ 2R³ = 1024

⇒ R³ = 512

⇒ R = ³√512 = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The amount of space inside a complete sphere is given by (4/3)πr³, where r is the radius.

Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The surface area of the curved part of a hemisphere is 2πr².

Total Surface Area of Hemisphere

Includes the base circle and the curved surface: 3πr².

Archimedes Principle in Volumes

When an object is submerged, it displaces a volume of liquid equal to its own volume.

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are (2x + 5)^circ, x^circ and (3x - 17)^circ . Find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any **triangle**, the sum of all interior angles is always **180°**.

Combine the **algebraic terms**: (2x + x + 3x) + (5 − 17) = 180

⇒ 6x − 12 = 180

⇒ 6x = 192

⇒ x = 32

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The angles of the triangle are (2x + 5)°, x° and (3x − 17)°.

**Formula Used:** **Angle Sum Property** of a triangle states that ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8f858bebcb560a555c428d1ef77aeb7de52d6d885e4089e63b8837cd1db6340.png] 

⇒ (2x + 5) + x + (3x − 17) = 180

⇒ 2x + x + 3x + 5 − 17 = 180

⇒ 6x − 12 = 180

⇒ 6x = 180 + 12

⇒ 6x = 192

⇒ x = 192 ÷ 6

⇒ x = 32

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any Euclidean triangle is always 180°, regardless of the triangle's shape or size.

Exterior Angle Theorem

An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles (Exterior ∠ = Interior Opposite ∠1 + Interior Opposite ∠2).

Types of Triangles by Angles

Triangles are classified as **Acute** (all angles 90°).

questions.question: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle PQR. AM and PS are altitudes and AN and PT are medians. If (AM)/(PS) = (3)/(5) , the area of triangle PQR is 150 { cm}² and BC = 6 { cm} , then the sum of the lengths of AM and QR is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of corresponding sides and altitudes of similar triangles is equal: **k** = AM/PS = BC/QR = 3/5.

Given **BC = 6 cm** ⇒ 6/QR = 3/5 ⇒ **QR = 10 cm**.

Area of ΔPQR = 1/2 × QR × PS = 150 ⇒ 1/2 × 10 × PS = 150 ⇒ 5 × PS = 150 ⇒ **PS = 30 cm**.

Altitude **AM** = (3/5) × PS = (3/5) × 30 = **18 cm**.

Sum = AM + QR = 18 + 10 = **28 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR

Ratio of altitudes AM/PS = 3/5

Area of ΔPQR = 150 cm²

Base BC of ΔABC = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

1. Ratio of areas of similar triangles = (Ratio of corresponding sides)² = (Ratio of altitudes)²

2. Area of triangle = 1/2 × base × height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/efa20f47d58256ff79305b94f1e96557c7a6958049c7cb32f5cde0d8589a66b7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For similar triangles, BC/QR = AM/PS = 3/5

⇒ 6 / QR = 3 / 5 ⇒ 3 × QR = 30 ⇒ QR = 10 cm

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = 1/2 × QR × PS = 150

⇒ 1/2 × 10 × PS = 150 ⇒ 5 × PS = 150 ⇒ PS = 30 cm

⇒ Since AM/PS = 3/5 ⇒ AM / 30 = 3 / 5 ⇒ AM = 18 cm

⇒ Sum = AM + QR = 18 + 10 = 28 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Areas of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides or linear dimensions (altitudes, medians, etc.): Area₁/Area₂ = (s₁/s₂)².

Similarity Ratios for Linear Components

For similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding sides, altitudes, medians, angle bisectors, and perimeters are all equal to the same constant factor **k**.

Median-Side Relation

In similar triangles ΔABC and ΔPQR, if AN and PT are medians, then AN/PT = BC/QR = AB/PQ = AC/PR = k.

questions.question: Given that 112⁰.¹⁷ = x , 112⁰.⁹⁴ = y and x^z = y⁶ , then the value of z is close to:

Directly equate the **exponents** by expressing **x** and **y** in terms of the common **base 112**.

Equation: (112⁰.¹⁷)z = (112⁰.⁹⁴)⁶

⇒ 0.17 × **z** = 0.94 × 6

⇒ **z** = 5.64 ÷ 0.17 ≈ 33.18

**∴ The correct answer is 33.18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = 112⁰.¹⁷

y = 112⁰.⁹⁴

xz = y⁶

**Formula Used:**

(am)ⁿ = am × ⁿ

If ap = aq, then p = q (for a > 0, a ≠ 1)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Substitute the values of **x** and **y** into the given equation xz = y⁶:

⇒ (112⁰.¹⁷)z = (112⁰.⁹⁴)⁶

⇒ 112⁽⁰.¹⁷ × z⁾ = 112⁽⁰.⁹⁴ × ⁶⁾

⇒ Since the **bases** are identical (112), we equate the **powers**:

⇒ 0.17 × z = 5.64

⇒ z = 5.64 ÷ 0.17

⇒ z = 564 ÷ 17

⇒ z ≈ 33.17647...

⇒ z ≈ 33.18

**∴ The correct answer is 33.18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Laws of Indices

When multiplying the same **base**, add **exponents**: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ. When dividing, subtract them: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ.

Power of a Power Rule

(am)ⁿ = am×ⁿ. This rule is fundamental for simplifying **exponential expressions** where a power is raised to another power.

Equating Powers

If the **base** on both sides of an equation is the same, their **powers** must be equal to satisfy the equation (assuming the base is not 0, 1, or −1).

The following table represents the marks obtained by six students in an aptitude test. Study the data carefully and answer the questions given below by matching the following types.

 Student A B C D E F
 Marks 48 50 52 55 60 65
Match the following (standard deviation values are rounded off to two decimal places):

 A. Standard deviation of entire dataset I. 5.88
 B. Standard deviation of only the middle four values (B, C, D, E) II. 3.77
 C. Standard deviation of only first three values (A, B, C) III. 4.08
 D. Standard deviation of only last three values (D, E, F) IV. 1.63

options.text: A − I, B − II, C − IV, D − III
A − II, B − IV, C − III, D − I
A − I, B − II, C − III, D − IV
A − II, B − IV, C − I, D − III

questions.solution:
**Given:**

 
 Student Marks Obtained
 
 **A** 48
 
 **B** 50
 
 **C** 52
 
 **D** 55
 
 **E** 60
 
 **F** 65

**Formula Used:**

1. **Mean (μ)** = (Σx) ÷ n

2. **Standard Deviation (σ)** = √[Σ(x − μ)² ÷ n]

**Calculation:**

**A. Standard deviation of entire dataset (A, B, C, D, E, F):**

⇒ Values: 48, 50, 52, 55, 60, 65

⇒ **Mean (μA)** = (48 + 50 + 52 + 55 + 60 + 65) ÷ 6 = 330 ÷ 6 = 55

⇒ Sum of squared deviations = (48−55)² + (50−55)² + (52−55)² + (55−55)² + (60−55)² + (65−55)²

⇒ Sum = (−7)² + (−5)² + (−3)² + (0)² + (5)² + (10)² = 49 + 25 + 9 + 0 + 25 + 100 = 208

⇒ **Standard Deviation (σA)** = √(208 ÷ 6) = √34.67 ≈ 5.88 (Matches **I**)

**B. Standard deviation of only the middle four values (B, C, D, E):**

⇒ Values: 50, 52, 55, 60

⇒ **Mean (μB)** = (50 + 52 + 55 + 60) ÷ 4 = 217 ÷ 4 = 54.25

⇒ Sum of squared deviations = (50−54.25)² + (52−54.25)² + (55−54.25)² + (60−54.25)²

⇒ Sum = (−4.25)² + (−2.25)² + (0.75)² + (5.75)² = 18.0625 + 5.0625 + 0.5625 + 33.0625 = 56.75

⇒ **Standard Deviation (σB)** = √(56.75 ÷ 4) = √14.1875 ≈ 3.77 (Matches **II**)

**C. Standard deviation of only first three values (A, B, C):**

⇒ Values: 48, 50, 52

⇒ **Mean (μC)** = (48 + 50 + 52) ÷ 3 = 150 ÷ 3 = 50

⇒ Sum of squared deviations = (48−50)² + (50−50)² + (52−50)² = 4 + 0 + 4 = 8

⇒ **Standard Deviation (σC)** = √(8 ÷ 3) = √2.67 ≈ 1.63 (Matches **IV**)

**D. Standard deviation of only last three values (D, E, F):**

⇒ Values: 55, 60, 65

⇒ **Mean (μD)** = (55 + 60 + 65) ÷ 3 = 180 ÷ 3 = 60

⇒ Sum of squared deviations = (55−60)² + (60−60)² + (65−60)² = 25 + 0 + 25 = 50

⇒ **Standard Deviation (σD)** = √(50 ÷ 3) = √16.67 ≈ 4.08 (Matches **III**)

**Matching Results:**

⇒ A → I, B → II, C → IV, D → III

**∴ The correct answer is Option (1).**

questions.question: Find the product of all the possible values of ‘a’ for a²x² + a³/²x + 3 = 0 to be a quadratic equation with discriminant 28a.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **a²x² + a³/²x + 3 = 0** to be a **quadratic equation**, **a² ≠ 0 ⇒ a ≠ 0**.

Discriminant **D = B² − 4AC = (a³/²)² − 4(a²)(3) = a³ − 12a²**.

Given **D = 28a ⇒ a³ − 12a² − 28a = 0**.

Factorizing: **a(a² − 12a − 28) = a(a − 14)(a + 2) = 0**.

Possible values of **a** are **14** and **−2** (excluding **a = 0**).

Product of values = **14 × (−2) = −28**.

**∴ The correct answer is −28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equation:** a²x² + a³/²x + 3 = 0

**Condition for Quadratic Equation:**

For any equation **Ax² + Bx + C = 0** to be quadratic, the coefficient of **x²** must not be zero.

⇒ **A ≠ 0**

⇒ **a² ≠ 0 ⇒ a ≠ 0**

**Discriminant Calculation:**

questions.question: If the sum of the 8th and the 12th terms of an AP is 100, and the 20th term is 95, then what is the 7th term?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the average of two terms equidistant from a middle term is the middle term itself: T₈ + T₁₂ = 2 × T₁₀.

⇒ 2 × T₁₀ = 100 ⇒ **T₁₀ = 50**.

Common difference (d) = (T₂₀ − T₁₀) ÷ (20 − 10) = (95 − 50) ÷ 10 = **4.5**.

Required term T₇ = T₁₀ − 3d = 50 − (3 × 4.5) = 50 − 13.5 = 36.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the **first term** be **a** and the **common difference** be **d**.

**Formula:** Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e77f94a926004db57e3006428e279a26ab4ed3fc55ea719f8fdfa40e9c7f38b4.png] 

**Given:**

Sum of **8th** and **12th terms** = 100

⇒ (a + 7d) + (a + 11d) = 100

⇒ 2a + 18d = 100 ⇒ a + 9d = 50 → (Eq. 1)

**20th term** = 95

⇒ a + 19d = 95 → (Eq. 2)

Subtract (Eq. 1) from (Eq. 2):

⇒ (a + 19d) − (a + 9d) = 95 − 50

⇒ 10d = 45 ⇒ **d = 4.5**

Substitute **d** in (Eq. 1):

⇒ a + 9 × 4.5 = 50

⇒ a + 40.5 = 50 ⇒ **a = 9.5**

To find the **7th term (T₇)**:

⇒ T₇ = a + 6d

⇒ T₇ = 9.5 + 6 × 4.5

⇒ T₇ = 9.5 + 27 = 36.5

**∴ The correct answer is 36.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Term of an AP

The nth term of an AP is given by Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where 'a' is the first term and 'd' is the common difference.

Sum of Equidistant Terms

In any finite AP, the sum of terms equidistant from the beginning and the end is constant: Tₖ + Tₙ−ₖ₊₁ = T₁ + Tₙ.

Arithmetic Mean (AM)

If three numbers x, y, z are in AP, then y = (x + z) ÷ 2. This is used here to find T₁₀ from T₈ and T₁₂.

questions.question:
In a test, Chris has to answer two questions. The probability that he will answer the first question correctly is (1)/(5) . If he answers the first question correctly, the probability that he will answer the second question correctly is (5)/(6) . If Chris does not answer the first question correctly, the probability that he will answer the second question correctly is (1)/(4) . Find the probability that Chris will answer the second question INCORRECTLY.
[Note: Assume that each question will be answered— either correctly or incorrectly.]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required **Probability** = [P(Q1 Correct) × P(Q2 Incorrect | Q1 Correct)] + [P(Q1 Incorrect) × P(Q2 Incorrect | Q1 Incorrect)]

⇒ (1/5 × (1 − 5/6)) + ((1 − 1/5) × (1 − 1/4))

⇒ (1/5 × 1/6) + (4/5 × 3/4) = 1/30 + 3/5

⇒ (1 + 18) / 30 = 19/30

**∴ The correct answer is 19/30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Probability** of answering the **first question** correctly, P(Q1C) = 1/5

**Probability** of answering the **first question** incorrectly, P(Q1I) = 1 − 1/5 = 4/5

**Conditional Probability** of answering the **second question** correctly given the first is correct, P(Q2C|Q1C) = 5/6

**Conditional Probability** of answering the **second question** correctly given the first is incorrect, P(Q2C|Q1I) = 1/4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/096d3ac9969eb5ec52a0e6a2f2722f33cc325d44731b37d77d8327fc02009533.png] 

**Formula Used:**

P(Q2I) = P(Q1C ∩ Q2I) + P(Q1I ∩ Q2I)

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Case 1:** Chris answers **Q1 correctly** and **Q2 incorrectly**.

⇒ P(Path A) = P(Q1C) × [1 − P(Q2C|Q1C)]

⇒ P(Path A) = 1/5 × (1 − 5/6) = 1/5 × 1/6 = 1/30

⇒ **Case 2:** Chris answers **Q1 incorrectly** and **Q2 incorrectly**.

⇒ P(Path B) = P(Q1I) × [1 − P(Q2C|Q1I)]

⇒ P(Path B) = 4/5 × (1 − 1/4) = 4/5 × 3/4 = 3/5

⇒ **Total Probability:** P(Q2I) = 1/30 + 3/5

⇒ P(Q2I) = (1 + 18) / 30 = 19/30

**∴ The correct answer is 19/30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Law of Total Probability

It expresses the total probability of an outcome which can be realized via several distinct events: P(A) = ∑ P(A|Bᵢ) × P(Bᵢ).

Conditional Probability

The probability of event A occurring given that event B has already occurred: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B).

Complementary Events

The sum of the probability of an event and its complement is always 1: P(E) + P(E′) = 1.</p

questions.question: Find the coordinates of a point P on the x-axis which is equidistant from the points A(2,3) and B(–4,5).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since point **P(x, 0)** is equidistant from **A(2, 3)** and **B(−4, 5)**, we equate the squared distances.

(x − 2)² + 3² = (x + 4)² + 5²

⇒ x² − 4x + 13 = x² + 8x + 41

⇒ 12x = −28

⇒ x = −7/3

**∴ The correct answer is (−7/3, 0).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Points **A(2, 3)** and **B(−4, 5)**. Point **P** lies on the **x-axis**.

**Formula used:** Distance d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1968b7243da3b849e24f35255ee3b234762456bd564cd8280ab15e81a7b7985c.png] 

Since **P** is on the **x-axis**, its coordinates are **(x, 0)**. Let **PA = PB**.

⇒ PA² = PB²

⇒ (x − 2)² + (0 − 3)² = (x − (−4))² + (0 − 5)²

⇒ (x − 2)² + (−3)² = (x + 4)² + (−5)²

⇒ x² − 4x + 4 + 9 = x² + 8x + 16 + 25

⇒ −4x + 13 = 8x + 41

⇒ −4x − 8x = 41 − 13

⇒ −12x = 28

⇒ x = −28 ÷ 12 = −7/3

**∴ The correct answer is (−7/3, 0).**

**__Additional Information__**

Point on Axis

Any point on the **x-axis** has a y-coordinate of 0, represented as (x, 0). Conversely, any point on the **y-axis** has an x-coordinate of 0, represented as (0, y).

Distance Formula

The distance between two points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).

Perpendicular Bisector

A point **equidistant** from two given points always lies on the **perpendicular bisector** of the line segment joining those two points.</p

questions.question: If X and Y are two sets such that X cup Y has 56 elements, X has 45 elements and Y has 33 elements, how many elements does X cap Y have ?

Inclusion-Exclusion Principle

For any two finite sets A and B, the cardinality of the union is given by n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).

Disjoint Sets

If two sets have no elements in common, they are **disjoint**, meaning n(A ∩ B) = 0 and n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B).

Difference of Sets

The number of elements belonging strictly to set X but not set Y is given by n(X − Y) = n(X) − n(X ∩ Y).</p

questions.question: If the roots of the equation x² - 5x + 6 = 0 are alpha and beta , find the value of alpha² + beta² :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Factorize the **quadratic equation** directly to find the roots.

For **x² − 5x + 6 = 0**, the factors are **(x − 2)(x − 3) = 0**.

The roots are **α = 2** and **β = 3**.

Now, calculate the sum of their squares: **2² + 3² = 4 + 9 = 13**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The equation is **x² − 5x + 6 = 0** where roots are **α** and **β**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of roots **(α + β) = −b/a** and Product of roots **(αβ) = c/a**.

⇒ From the equation, **a = 1**, **b = −5**, and **c = 6**.

⇒ Sum of roots **(α + β) = −(−5)/1 = 5**

⇒ Product of roots **(αβ) = 6/1 = 6**

⇒ We know that **(α + β)² = α² + β² + 2αβ**

⇒ **5² = α² + β² + 2 × 6**

⇒ **25 = α² + β² + 12**

⇒ **α² + β² = 25 − 12**

⇒ **α² + β² = 13**

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Roots and Coefficients

For a quadratic equation **ax² + bx + c = 0**, the sum is **−b/a** and the product is **c/a**.

Nature of Roots

The discriminant **D = b² − 4ac** determines the nature: if **D > 0** roots are real and distinct, if **D = 0** roots are real and equal.

Higher Power Identities

The sum of cubes of roots is **α³ + β³ = (α + β)(α² + β² − αβ)** or **(α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β)**.</p

questions.question: The number of elements in the Power set P(S) of the set S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8} is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The number of elements in the **power set** of any set with **n** elements is always 2ⁿ.

In this problem, the set **S** has 8 elements (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8).

Number of elements in **P(S)** = 2⁸

2⁸ = 256

**∴ The correct answer is 256.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Set S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}

Number of elements in set S, n(S) = 8

**Formula Used:**

Total number of elements in Power Set P(S) = 2ⁿ⁽S⁾

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5995d2714d5e7a328194d5ea13a6e163fe0cf1425a633f39fac115c76b7c6cf5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of elements in the given set S = 8

⇒ Power set P(S) is the set of all **subsets** of S.

⇒ Number of elements in P(S) = 2⁸

⇒ 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 256

**∴ The correct answer is 256.**

**__Additional Information__**

Power Set Definition

The set consisting of all **possible subsets** of a set A is called the power set of A, denoted as P(A). It includes the **null set (φ)** and the set itself.

Proper Subsets

A subset that is not equal to the original set is a **proper subset**. The number of proper subsets is 2ⁿ − 1.

Non-Empty Subsets

The number of **non-empty subsets** of a set with n elements is given by the formula 2ⁿ − 1.</p

questions.question: In a PNP transistor, an increase in collector–base reverse bias causes a slight increase in collector current even when the emitter current is held constant. This occurs primarily because:

questions.question: Two conductors of the same material have lengths L and 2L and equal resistance. The ratio of their cross-sectional areas ( A₁:A₂ ) is _______.

__**Concept:**__

The resistance of a conductor is given by,

R=(rho L)/(A)

where,

R = resistance of the conductor

ρ = resistivity of the material

L = length of the conductor

A = cross-sectional area of the conductor

__**Calculation:**__

__**Given:**__

Length of first conductor = L

Length of second conductor = 2L

Resistance of both conductors is equal.

For the first conductor,

R=(rho L)/(A₁)

For the second conductor,

R=(rho (2L))/(A₂)

Since the resistances are equal,

(rho L)/(A₁)=(rho (2L))/(A₂)

Cancelling ρ and L from both sides,

(1)/(A₁)=(2)/(A₂)

A₂=2A₁

Therefore,

A₁:A₂=1:2

__**Answer:**__

**Option (2) : 1 : 2**

questions.question: When several resistors are connected in series, which physical quantity has an identical value across each resistor?

__
 
• When resistors are connected in series__, the current passing through each resistor is the same.
 
• This is because in a series connection, there is only one path for the current to flow.
 
• In contrast, the voltage across each resistor in series varies based on their resistance values.
 
• The total resistance of the series combination is the sum of the individual resistances.
 
• Examples of series circuits include string lights where if one bulb fails, the entire circuit is broken.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Series vs Parallel Circuits:**

 
 
• In a series circuit, the current remains the same, but the voltage divides among components.
 
• In a parallel circuit, the voltage remains constant across all branches, but the current divides.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that V = I × R, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• This fundamental principle helps analyze both series and parallel circuits.

questions.question: A logic function is given by F = ABC + DE. You are allowed to use only two input AND gates and NOT gates. How many minimum number of two input AND gates and how many minimum number of NOT gates are required to implement this function?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

To implement a given logic function using a minimum number of basic gates, we can transform the expression using De Morgan's Laws to eliminate unsupported operations (like the OR operation) so that it only contains multiplications (AND) and inversions (NOT).

De Morgan's Law states that:

overline{X + Y} = overline{X} · overline{Y}

For a function with multiple inputs, a double inversion is applied to keep the value identical while rewriting the operations:

F = overline{overline{F}}

__**Calculation:**__

__**Given:**__

Logic function: F = ABC + DE

Allowed gates: Only 2-input AND gates and NOT gates.

**Step 1: Convert the function using De Morgan's Laws**

Apply double inversion to remove the OR operation:

F = overline{overline{ABC + DE}}

Applying De Morgan's Law inside the first inversion yields:

F = overline{(overline{ABC}) · (overline{DE})}

**Step 2: Gate Counting Analysis**

1. Implementing the term ABC using 2-input AND gates:

 
• First 2-input AND gate: X = A · B
 
• Second 2-input AND gate: Y = X · C = ABC

*(Requires 2 AND gates)*

2. Implementing the term DE using a 2-input AND gate:

 
• Third 2-input AND gate: Z = D · E = DE

*(Requires 1 AND gate)*

3. Inverting the intermediate products:

 
• First NOT gate: overline{ABC}
 
• Second NOT gate: overline{DE}

*(Requires 2 NOT gates)*

4. Combining the inverted components with an AND operation:

 
• Fourth 2-input AND gate: W = (overline{ABC}) · (overline{DE})

*(Requires 1 AND gate)*

5. Performing the final external inversion:

 
• Third NOT gate: F = overline{W} = overline{(overline{ABC}) · (overline{DE})}

*(Requires 1 NOT gate)*

**Conclusion:**

Total 2-input AND gates needed = 2 + 1 + 1 = **4 AND gates**

Total NOT gates needed = 2 + 1 = **3 NOT gates**

questions.question: The resistivity of a semiconductor decreases with the increase in temperature because:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resistivity__ of a semiconductor is inversely related to the number of charge carriers.
 
• When temperature increases, the energy supplied to the semiconductor increases.
 
• This leads to breaking of covalent bonds and generation of more electron-hole pairs.
 
• The increase in charge carriers reduces the semiconductor’s resistivity.
 
• Unlike conductors, where resistivity increases with temperature, semiconductors exhibit a decrease in resistivity due to this behavior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Band Gap:**

 
 
• The band gap of a semiconductor remains constant for a specific material and does not increase with temperature.
 
• However, higher temperatures provide energy for electrons to jump the band gap, generating more carriers.
 
 
 
• **Lattice Vibrations:**
 
 
• Lattice vibrations increase with temperature but do not stop entirely.
 
• Lattice vibrations primarily affect conductivity in metals rather than in semiconductors.
 
 
 
• **Electrons Lose Energy:**
 
 
• Electrons gain energy at higher temperatures rather than losing it, enabling them to move to the conduction band.

questions.question: Port 0 of the 8051 microcontroller differs architecturally from the other ports primarily because:

questions.question: Ohm’s law may NOT hold true when _____.

options.text: The temperature of the conductor remains constant

__
 
• Ohm’s law__ states that the current passing through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across its ends, provided physical conditions such as temperature remain constant.
 
• If the temperature of the conductor changes, the resistivity of the material changes, and Ohm’s law may not hold true.
 
• Ohm’s law is applicable only to ohmic materials such as metals, which exhibit a linear V-I relationship.
 
• When the material is non-ohmic, such as semiconductors or diodes, the V-I graph is nonlinear, and Ohm’s law does not apply.
 
• In metallic conductors, temperature changes significantly affect resistance and thus violate Ohm’s law.

• Temperature: An increase in temperature increases resistance in metallic conductors, making the V-I relationship nonlinear.
 
• Type of Material: Non-ohmic materials like semiconductors and insulators do not obey Ohm’s law.
 
 
 
• **Ohmic and Non-Ohmic Materials:**
 
 
• Ohmic materials: Metals such as copper and aluminum follow a linear V-I relationship.
 
• Non-ohmic materials: Devices like diodes and transistors exhibit nonlinear behavior.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ohm’s Law:**
 
 
• Used to calculate resistance, current, or voltage in electrical circuits.
 
• Essential for designing and analyzing electrical and electronic systems.

questions.question: The SI unit of specific resistance (resistivity) is _______.

 **R = ρL/A**

• **Resistance (R)** is measured in **ohm (Ω)**,
 
• **Area (A)** in **m²**, and
 
• **Length (L)** in **m**,
 
 the SI unit of resistivity becomes:

 **Ω × m²/m = Ω·m (ohm-metre)**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Option 3 – ohm-metre.***

• SI Unit: **siemens per metre (S/m)**.

questions.question: An ideal half-wave rectifier supplies a purely resistive load from a sinusoidal source. Let v_L(t) be the load voltage and v_D(t) be the diode voltage, measured with reference to the anode. Which of the following statements is always true over one complete cycle?

options.text: The average value of v_D(t) becomes zero if the diode orientation is reversed.
The average values of v_L(t) and v_D(t) are equal in magnitude and opposite in sign.
The rms value of v_D(t) equals the rms value of the source voltage.
The average value of v_D(t) is zero because the diode conducts for half the cycle.

questions.question: In 8051 microcontroller, PSEN is an _____ output signal used as a read strobe for accessing the _____ memory.

• The PSEN pin plays a crucial role in accessing this external memory.

questions.question: Two resistors 6 Omega and 3 Omega are connected in parallel. The total resistance is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __2 Ω**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula for total resistance__ in a parallel circuit is:
 
• 1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.
 
• Substitute R₁ = 6 Ω and R₂ = 3 Ω into the formula:
 
• 1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/6 + 1/3 = (1 + 2)/6 = 3/6 = 1/2.
 
• Therefore, Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 2 Ω.
 
• The correct total resistance is 2 Ω.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Parallel Circuit:**
 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each resistor is the same.
 
• The total resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance.
 
 
 
• **Series Circuit:**
 
 
• In a series circuit, the current through each resistor is the same.
 
• The total resistance is the sum of individual resistances.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• It is used to calculate electrical parameters in circuits.

questions.question: A resistor of 10 Omega is connected to a constant voltage source. When another resistor is connected in series with it, the current in the circuit becomes half of its initial value. Assuming the supply voltage remains unchanged, the resistance of the second resistor is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __10 Ω**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The initial resistance of the circuit is 10 Ω.
 
• When another resistor is connected in series, the current becomes half of its initial value.
 
• In a series circuit, the total resistance is the sum of all resistors.
 
• Let the second resistor's resistance be R.
 
• From Ohm's Law, the current is inversely proportional to the resistance if the voltage remains constant.
 
• Initially, resistance = 10 Ω, and after adding R, the total resistance becomes 10 + R.
 
• Since the current is halved, the new resistance is 2 times the initial resistance.
 
• Thus, 10 + R = 2 × 10, giving R = 10 Ω.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It states that V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• In a series circuit, the total resistance is the sum of individual resistances.
 
 
 
• **Current in Series Circuits:**
 
 
• The current remains constant throughout all components in a series circuit.
 
• The voltage across each resistor depends on its resistance value.

questions.question: If a uniform magnetic field is parallel to the plane of a surface, the magnetic flux through the surface is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __zero.__

__
 
• Magnetic flux__ is defined as the total number of magnetic field lines passing through a given surface.
 
• When the magnetic field is parallel to the plane of the surface, the angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the surface is 90°.
 
• The magnetic flux is given by Φ = B × A × cos θ, where θ is the angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the surface.
 
• For θ = 90°, cos 90° = 0, therefore the magnetic flux becomes zero.
 
• This means no magnetic field lines pass through the surface in this orientation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Flux:**

 
 
• It is a scalar quantity represented by Φ.
 
• SI unit of magnetic flux is Weber (Wb).
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field:**
 
 
• It is a vector quantity that represents the region around a magnetic material where magnetic forces can be observed.
 
• The SI unit of magnetic field is Tesla (T).

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental (base) quantity in the SI system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mass__ is one of the seven fundamental (base) quantities in the SI system.
 
• The SI unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).
 
• Fundamental quantities are those that are not derived from other quantities; they serve as the foundation for other measurements.
 
• Other examples of fundamental quantities include length, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.
 
• Derived quantities, like work, force, and pressure, are expressed in terms of these fundamental quantities.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Work:**

 
 
• Work is a derived quantity and is measured in joules (J).
 
• It is calculated as the product of force and displacement.
 
 
 
• **Pressure:**
 
 
• Pressure is a derived quantity and is measured in pascals (Pa).
 
• It is defined as force per unit area.
 
 
 
• **Force:**
 
 
• Force is also a derived quantity and is measured in newtons (N).
 
• It is calculated using Newton's second law of motion: F = ma.
